column1: In this chapter we take the economy’s factors of production as given. In other words, we assume that the economy has a fixed amount of capital and a fixed amount of labor. We write K  K – . L  L – . The overbar means that each variable is fixed at some level. In Chapter 8 we examine what happens when the factors of production change over time, as they do in the real world. For now, to keep our analysis simple, we assume fixed amounts of capital and labor.
